Building my first AR and I have a technical question.

A couple notes:

1) If you're going 16", go 5.56 instead. 300blk was designed for short barreled weapons and for running subsonic suppressed. 5.56 was designed for longer barrels.

2) If you want 300blk go with an 8-10" barrel and run it with a pistol brace.

3) If you're talking "sniper" class, consider an AR10 because 308 is a much better long range anti-personnel round than 5.56 or 300blk. If you already have parts for AR15, go with 224 Valkyrie if you hate your wallet and 5.56 if you don't.

4) Pistol length gas system if you build a pistol, rifle length if you go with 16" or longer.

Do you think I should opt for an 18in 556 barrel if I want this to be a long range focused rifle? What’s a good twist ratio for a 16 or 18 inch barrel?

18" is a nice length for longer ranges with 5.56 for sure, you'll get a lot of muzzle velocity and your trajectory should be relatively predictable out to a couple hundred yards.

Twist rate is mostly about what bullet weight you want to run. An aggressive twist rate is better for heavier bullets, but too aggressive and it can cause issues with lighter bullets like a 55gr. If you're wanting to reach out further, you'll probably want to step up to a little heavier bullets, so I'd suggest probably 1-in-8 or 1-in-7. Both will reliably stabilize 55gr while also working well with heavier bullets up to 75gr or so.

Also, I'm not sure what your experience is with longer range shooting, but know that quality ammo goes a long way, especially in rifles. A really high quality match-grade bullet certainly won't turn your average carbine into a tack driver, but low quality ammo can make a tack driver much less accurate.
Thanks for the knowledge. I ordered a 1:8.

Pistol gas system if you want to run subsonic ammo and carbine if you want to use supersonic. Pistol will run both but may overgas on hotter ammo meaning you might need an adjustable gas system, or heavier buffer. If you truly want a 300 black consider that it's only really good for about 400 yards at best. That being said it is a great round for hunting. If you want long range from an ar platform just about any other caliber will better than 300 blk which is essentially a .45 acp with subsonic loadings.

It looks like this is the rifle in the film: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boys_anti-tank_rifle

From the article: "Although adequate against light tanks and tankettes in the early part of the war, the Boys was ineffective against heavier armour and was phased out in favour of the PIAT mid-war."

As far as penetration it had: "23.2mm penetration at 90° 100 yards (91 m)"

Also from the article:

"Although useful against early German and Italian tanks in France and North Africa, as well as in the Norwegian campaign, such as the Panzer I, Panzer II and early models of Panzer III, increases in vehicle armour during the Second World War left the Boys largely ineffectual as an anti-tank weapon. A shortened version was issued in 1942 for issue to airborne forces and saw use in Tunisia, where it proved completely ineffective because of the reduced velocity caused by the shortened barrel.[6] Another limitation was that the Boys rifle was relatively heavy and unwieldy to carry and set up.[citation needed]

The Boys reputation after the Battle of France was such that the Canadian government, through the Directorate of Military Training, The Department of National Defence and National Film Board of Canada (NFB) commissioned a training film, Stop That Tank! (1942), from Walt Disney Studios to counter the rifle's "jinx" reputation.

Nonetheless, in the European theatre it was soon replaced by the PIAT (Projector, Infantry, Anti-Tank) in 1943, which first saw service during the Allied invasion of Sicily. In other roles the Boys saw some use against bunkers, machine gun nests and light-skinned vehicles but was rapidly replaced in British and Commonwealth service, as quantities of the latter weapon became available, by the U.S. .50 BMG calibre M2 Browning machine gun."
